idee_recherchee.texte: Quantum entanglement links particles so that measuring one instantly affects the other no matter the distance, and some theorists believe that entanglement is the thread from which spacetime itself is woven.

titre_video: Scientists Are Freaking Out Over Space Time (It's Not Real)
titre: La mécanique quantique comme moteur physique bogué
resume: Quantum mechanics has particles popping in and out of existence, being in two places until measured, and affecting each other across light-years via entanglement. The narrator likens this to a glitchy physics engine of a simulation struggling with limited processing power.
texte: If the double slit experiment wasn't enough to fry your brain, quantum mechanics as a whole ignores common sense. At the atomic level, particles don't follow normal rules. They pop in and out of existence, teleport between locations, and seem to communicate instantly across vast distances. >> [music] >> Scientists call this quantum entanglement, but for our purposes, let's just call it what it is, a glitchy physics engine. Particles can randomly pop in and out of existence, just like data loading and unloading. Electrons are able to exist in two places at once until measured, as if the system hasn't fully rendered their position yet. And particles instantly affect each other across light-years, like a physics engine cutting corners to keep reality running smoothly. Quantum mechanics defies traditional physics, but if [music] reality is a programmed simulation, these bizarre behaviors start to make sense. Suddenly it looks like a limited system struggling to keep up with processing power.
